title: Mapping Visual-to-Language Feature Handoff in a Small Multimodal Model

original_idea.body:
# Mapping Visual-to-Language Feature Handoff in a Small Multimodal Model

**Problem:** How visual representations map into language feature space in multimodal LLMs is barely studied; where a safety-relevant visual concept becomes a language concept triggering refusal is unmapped.

**Direction:** Using a small open multimodal model and Prisma/SAE tooling, trace at which layer a visual feature aligns with the language concept and test whether refusal is driven by the visual or later language feature.

**Why it matters:** Image-driven jailbreaks exploit this handoff.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2506.11976; Prisma (arXiv 2504.19475).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (image-jailbreak handoff) but mapping-to-mitigation link has a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Multimodal feature tracing across modalities is intermediate; nontrivial tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused on one visual concept's handoff with a clear localization question.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, novel multimodal-safety work; lab-independent.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on a small multimodal model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The safety-concept visual-to-language handoff mapping appears largely unexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The safety-relevant visual-to-language handoff mapping appears largely unexplored.
